title: Proportional pin-drain coordinator for staged canary slicing with regional capacity awareness
creator: Jordan Klein
description:
Problem: When we perform staged canary/A-B rollouts with session or request-level model version pinning, existing drain strategies either (a) brute-force evict pinned sessions causing errors/latency spikes, or (b) keep pins indefinitely causing traffic skew and blocking canary progress. We need a coordinator that rebalances pinned affinity proportionally to the target canary weight while respecting regional tier capacity, reducing user-visible errors and minimizing cross-region traffic shifts.

Goal: Implement a Proportional Pin-Drain Coordinator (PPDC) that: 1) gradually migrates pinned sessions toward the desired variant proportion at a controllable rate, 2) honors region/tier routing policies and capacity constraints, 3) exposes safety gates and observability for rollback, and 4) integrates with rollout configs (canary percentages, A/B weights, stickiness TTLs).

Acceptance criteria:
- PPDC shifts pinned affinities so active assignment distribution matches target canary weight within +/-5% after configured transition window for non-evicted sessions.
- No >1% increase in 5xx errors attributable to pin migration on staging load test.
- Console shows live calibration metrics (pinned distribution, migration rate, blocked-by-capacity events) and supports pause/rollback.
- API supports per-route migration policy and per-customer overrides.

High-level approach:
- Coordinator component sits alongside the routing resolver; for each route it calculates desired pinned split given target weights and current pinned counts.
- Use proportional reclamation: mark a fraction of pins eligible for migration each epoch proportional to (current_share - target_share). Eligible pins are scheduled for gentle eviction (TTL shrink + rebind) rather than forced kill.
- Respect region and tier capacity by querying the capacity oracle; if a migration would exceed capacity in a region/tier, defer and enqueue with backpressure.
- Provide a soft-eviction path: on next request from an eligible pinned session we honor the new routing decision and transition KV state incrementally. This avoids abrupt user-visible failures for long-lived sessions.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive eviction reduces time-to-target but increases error surface and cache churn. We choose configurable conservative defaults (10% of excess pins per epoch) with an opt-in aggressive mode for emergency rollouts.
- Centralized coordinator simplifies global balancing but is a single logic point; we mitigate with sharded coordinators and leader-election in each region.
- Precise capacity forecasting is hard; we conservatively reserve headroom thresholds to avoid overloads during migration spikes.

Design notes / API changes:
- New route config fields: migration_window_seconds, migration_step_fraction, regional_capacity_margin, allow_aggressive_mode (boolean).
- Coordinator exposes endpoints: GET /v1/route/{id}/pin-metrics, POST /v1/route/{id}/migration/pause, POST /v1/route/{id}/migration/force-step.

Tasks (engineering):
- [ ] Implement PPDC core algorithm and epoch loop (ENG backend) - Priya
- [ ] Integrate with routing resolver to mark eligible pins and perform soft-evictions - Priya/Jordan
- [ ] Hook capacity oracle for region/tier checks - Marco Chen (infra)
- [ ] Add route config parsing and validation - SRE/Config team
- [ ] Console telemetry + controls (pause/step UI) - DES + PM
- [ ] E2E staging load tests with synthetic pinned sessions and canary targets - QE
- [ ] Docs + runbook + rollback playbook - PM/SRE

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Migration increases tail latency due to rebind work. Mitigation: rate-limit migration epochs and monitor P99; cutover pause on thresholds.
- Risk: Cross-region moves cause higher egress costs & regulatory issues. Mitigation: respect region pinning policy; never migrate a pin off a geo-locked customer without opt-in.

Observability plan:
- New metrics: pinned_count_{variant,route,region,tier}, eligible_for_migration_count, migration_steps_executed, migration_blocked_by_capacity, migration_error_rate.
- Dashboards: "Pin migration overview", per-route heatmap, and alerting: migration_error_rate > 0.5% for 5m, migration_blocked_by_capacity > 10% for 10m.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for proportional calculation, step scheduling, and capacity backoff logic.
- Integration test: simulated 100k active sessions across 3 regions, target canary set to 20% and validated that distribution reaches target within migration_window with no >1% error spike.
- Chaos tests: kill one region orchestrator mid-migration to verify coordinator requeues and continues safely.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag behind route-level opt-in in staging.
- Small-scale canary to internal customers (10 routes) for 48h.
- Gradual ramp: enable across customer tiers with monitoring gates and manual approval at each stage.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Proportional+Pin-Drain+Coordinator
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/2147
- Load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/pin-migration-staging

Open questions:
- Should we support per-customer policies that permanently opt out of migration? (PM to confirm legal/contractual constraints)
- How to surface cost impact per migration (eg. cross-region egress) in the Console?

Next steps:
- Finish core algorithm and a minimal API surface for pausing/stepping.
- Coordinate with Console team for a lightweight pause/step control.
- Schedule a review with PM and Design next Wed to lock defaults and opt-out semantics.
